title: Backpressure-aware partial aggregate store with staleness budgets for dashboard queries
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Background: Several dashboard endpoints serving time-range rollups are experiencing occasional high p99 tail latencies when cold or when many large-range queries arrive concurrently. Root cause analysis shows expensive shard scans that compute full aggregates per-request and a cache that stores only complete aggregates, leading to cache misses and high memory/CPU spikes under burst. This ticket introduces a partial-aggregate store that serves tranche-level aggregates, combined with per-query staleness budgets and a backpressure-aware admission policy to reduce full-scan frequency and smooth resource usage.
goals: Reduce dashboard p99 latency for range-rollup queries by >= 3x in bursty workloads
Cut full-scan CPU spike incidents by 70% for queries that can be answered by partial aggregates
Introduce configurable staleness budgets so teams can trade freshness for latency
Make the mechanism pluggable per-route and observable in Console metrics
success_metrics: p50/p95/p99 for affected endpoints compared to baseline (target p99 down 3x)
Number of full shard scans per minute reduced by >= 70% under synthetic bursts
Cache hit rate for partial aggregates >= 65% for representative production traces
No regression in median latency or error rate after rollout
acceptance_criteria: Partial-aggregate store implemented as a tier alongside existing full-aggregate cache
Per-route staleness budget configuration exposed in route config and respected by query planner
Backpressure admission limits queries that would force full scans under high CPU contention
Integration tests cover correctness of combined partial+full aggregate answers across time windows
Perf tests demonstrate target reductions on replayed production traffic in staging
Observability: Console dashboard shows partial-agg hit rate, CPU savings, and staleness breakdown
technical_design: Shard-level tranche buckets: precompute fixed-size time slices (eg 1m/5m) for each metric series and store incremental aggregates
Query planner checks tranche coverage for requested range; if covered and within staleness budget, return assembled partial-aggregate result without full scan
Staleness budget: per-route numeric TTL that allows returning cached tranche aggregates up to N seconds old; default conservative values provided

Backpressure admission: when CPU utilization or query-queue depth exceeds thresholds, planner refuses admission for queries that would trigger >X full-shard reads and returns graceful degraded response (partial-data + metadata) or schedules async refresh
Eviction and compaction: LRU by (tenant, metric) with size caps; compaction pipeline merges adjacent tranches to reduce memory after retention period
Compatibility: fall back to existing full-aggregate path when partial store is cold or disabled for a route
Pluggable policy hooks so Dedicated/private deployments can tune budgets and admission rules
implementation_tasks: Add tranche schema and write path in ingestion pipeline to emit tranche aggregates to store
Extend cache layer to index and retrieve by (tenant, metric, tranche-window)
Implement query planner changes: tranche coverage check + staleness evaluation
Implement backpressure detector using existing runtime telemetry (CPU, queue lengths)
Add config surfaces to route definitions and Console for staleness budgets and backpressure thresholds
Write unit and integration tests, and a load harness to replay production traces against staging
Instrument metrics and Console panels: partial-agg-hit-rate, tranche-coverage, admission-denied-count
tradeoffs_and_notes: Partial aggregates reduce compute but increase storage and ingestion work; we will limit tranche granularity and retention to control cost
Staleness budgets shift correctness to clients; will provide clear per-route metadata so callers can decide acceptable freshness
Backpressure denial returns partial data with metadata; some legacy clients might not handle degraded payloads—plan a compatibility flag
Compaction increases background CPU usage; schedule during off-peak windows and allow Dedicated tenants to opt out
rollout_plan: Feature gated behind runtime flag; enable for a non-critical tenant group first
Stage 1: Ingest tranches for a subset of metrics and enable read-path in canary region
Stage 2: Enable staleness budgets and backpressure admission for 10% of traffic, monitor metrics
Stage 3: Ramp to 50% then 100% across regions after validating perf and correctness
Rollback: disable read-path or force full-aggregate reads if correctness or error thresholds are exceeded
testing_plan: Unit tests for planner logic and staleness budget evaluation
Integration tests that compare assembled partial-aggregate results vs full-scan results across many random time ranges
Staging perf replay using two representative production windows: normal and burst
Chaos: induce high CPU and ensure backpressure admission triggers and graceful degraded responses
Long-running soak to validate compaction and eviction behavior
monitoring_and_alerts: Create Console dashboard for partial-agg metrics: hit rate, tranche writes/sec, compaction rate
Alert if partial-agg hit rate drops below 30% for a route or if admission-denied count > threshold
SLO: p99 latency not to exceed baseline * 1.2 during rollout; alert for regressions
Audit logs of when backpressure denied queries for postmortem investigations
